examples.question_text:
A pattern begins at $10$ when $x=1$ and decreases by $2$ each time $x$ increases by $1$. Complete the table, then choose the matching table.

$\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&10&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots\end{array}$

$A=\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&10&8&6&4\end{array}$

$B=\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&10&9&8&7\end{array}$
examples.solution_text:
Subtract $2$ for each increase of $1$ in $x$.

$\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&10&8&6&4\end{array}$

Table $A$ has the same starting value and decrease.

examples.question_text:
Use $y=-2x+3$ to complete the table.

$\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&0&1&2&3\\\hline y&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots&\ldots\end{array}$

examples.solution_text:
The marked points are $(0,1)$, $(1,3)$, $(2,5)$ and $(3,7)$.

$\begin{array}{c|cccc}x&0&1&2&3\\\hline y&1&3&5&7\end{array}$

Table $A$ matches every marked point.

Both equations give $y=5$ at $x=0$. Read another marked point: $(1,3)$.

For $y=-2x+5$ at $x=1$:

$\begin{aligned}y&=-2(1)+5\\&=3\end{aligned}$

For $y=-x+5$ at $x=1$:

$\begin{aligned}y&=-(1)+5\\&=4\end{aligned}$

The graph matches $y=-2x+5$. Its other marked points, $(2,1)$ and $(3,-1)$, also agree with this equation.

examples.question_text:
Find the equation represented by the table. Check the column for $x=8$.

$\begin{array}{c|cccccc}x&0&1&2&3&4&8\\\hline y&-4&-1&2&5&8&20\end{array}$
examples.solution_text:
For each increase of $1$ in $x$, $y$ increases by $3$. At $x=0$, $y=-4$.

$y=3x-4$

For $x=8$:

$\begin{aligned}y&=3(8)-4\\&=20\end{aligned}$

This agrees with the table.

Read the marked points to make a table.

$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&-1&0&1&2&3\\\hline y&4&2&0&-2&-4\end{array}$

For each increase of $1$ in $x$, $y$ decreases by $2$. The graph crosses the $y$-axis at $(0,2)$.

$y=-2x+2$

methods.description: Use the starting value and constant increase or decrease to complete or select a table.
Substitute each listed x-value into the equation to obtain its corresponding y-value.
Read coordinates from the graph and place each pair in a table column; compare all listed pairs when selecting a table.
Read graph coordinates and compare the y-values produced by candidate equations at the same x-values.

methods.description: Use the constant change in y for each unit increase in x and the y-value at x=0 to form the equation; check an additional column.

coverage.summary: Authored six examples covering the distinct accepted assessment methods, combining increasing/decreasing and completion/selection variants where the method is shared. All examples separate prompts from solutions, use editable inline mathematics and supported TikZ, and rely on automatic blue solution styling. Continuation rows align at equals signs; no bare opening expressions require phantom gutters. Graph givens remain in prompts, with derived coordinates and explanations in solutions. Practice and quiz mathematics were neither changed nor re-audited. Independent review of the new examples and actual rendered typography/layout verification remain for subsequent stages.

examples.derivation: Starting at 10 and subtracting 2 gives 10, 8, 6, 4. Table A matches both the starting value and constant decrease. This adapts the decreasing pattern in source question 6.
Substitution into y=-2x+3 for x=0,1,2,3 gives 3,1,-1,-3. Every intermediate calculation and table entry agrees. This follows the equation-to-table task in source question 15.
The plotted rule y=2x+1 gives the marked coordinates (0,1), (1,3), (2,5), (3,7). These produce the completed table and match A. Reading marked coordinates into a table follows source questions 11–12.

Both candidates give 5 at x=0. At x=1, -2(1)+5=3 whereas -(1)+5=4. The plotted points (2,1) and (3,-1) also satisfy y=-2x+5. The comparison uses equivalent graph coordinates and equation values within the supplied source approach and accepted assessed method.
Successive unit increases in x increase y by 3, and the x=0 entry is -4, giving y=3x-4. The additional column checks as 3(8)-4=20. This adapts source question 9.

The plotted coordinates are (-1,4), (0,2), (1,0), (2,-2), (3,-4). Each unit increase in x decreases y by 2, and the intercept is 2, giving y=-2x+2. All table entries agree with the plot. This follows source question 13.

New examples use different values, remain within scope, separate prompts and solutions, and preserve editable prose with automatic blue solution styling. No phantom gutters are required. Diagram coordinates, authored palette and font settings are consistent; actual rendered typography and layout remain for the later visual stage. No syllabus exception or solid-geometry review is needed. Accepted practice and quiz mathematics were not re-audited.
